provenance.baseline_policy: hold SPY over the identical next-open-to-10-session-close window for every exposure row; excess_10d = exposure-ticker window return minus SPY window return, materialized per row by the wired observer

expectation_gap.gap_definition: The SPY-carry prior treats theme-peers of negative-event and positive-event names as identically priced exposures, while the replay evidence (exp-20260702-021 baseline-controlled, exp-20260703-005 reversal-controlled) claims negative-event theme-peers earn HIGHER ten-session SPY-excess than positive-event theme-peers because intra-theme capital rotates toward untouched peers after adverse first-order news.

transmission.catalyst: A structured first-order news event with machine-recorded polarity joined through the deterministic entity-exposure map to listed theme-peers before the next session open.
transmission.expected_direction: Negative-side peer rows settle with higher excess_10d than positive-side peer rows at both event and row level if the rotation mechanism is real out of replay.
transmission.half_life: From the event's next regular session open through the tenth following session close.

candidate_snapshots.why_not_arbitraged: The claim is a diffuse second-order cross-sectional tilt, not a first-order headline trade: peers are one join away from the news, the direction is inverted relative to naive sentiment reading, and the replay magnitude carried a suspicious right tail, so fast money has no obvious reason to crowd it. Monetization would require a shared-paper-first default-off tilt helper with an execution envelope that does not exist yet; this read allocates no capital and changes no order.
candidate_snapshots.falsifier: Reject the forward-validation claim unless ALL of the following hold on the frozen cohort: (1) outcome-blind floors already verified - negative closed rows >= 200, negative events >= 20, negative event dates >= 10, positive control rows >= 200; (2) event-level primary - mean of per-event mean excess_10d for negative events exceeds the same statistic for positive events; (3) row-level - pooled mean AND pooled median excess_10d negative > positive; (4) chronological stability - splitting each side's events at its median event_date, the event-level negative-minus-positive separation is positive in BOTH halves; (5) concentration - no single negative event contributes more than 40% of the negative side's summed positive per-event mean excess, and no single exposure ticker contributes more than 40% of the negative side's row-level positive excess mass. A full pass is still only observed_only and promotes no pool, tilt, or order; any fail re-parks the lane with a redeclared quantitative bar.
